newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, further weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, further weakness seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.26 percent on Wednesday, pushed down by a lack of active participation and concerns the new tax on profits from securities would continue to weigh down the market.
"We're happy that trading closed for today, because if it would continue like this, the outlook would be even more miserable," said Ljudmila Bojec, a trader at brokers Dolenjska.
Traders see further weakness ahead of the year-end.
* The 10-share SBI index fell 3.03 points to 1,160.3.
* Overall nine shares fell, five rose and three were unchanged, while another eight were untraded.
* Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 0.43 percent to 41,820 tolars on volume of 3,316 shares.
